current_date: 2024 (from the council page's link title 'Planning application requirements local list 2024'; the PDF text itself gives no adoption/publication date)
current_evidence: The council page 'What you need to submit with your planning application' (beta.southglos.gov.uk/what-you-need-to-submit-with-your-planning-application/) links this exact PDF as 'Planning application requirements local list 2024' alongside the 'National planning application requirements November 2019' document; no newer list is linked.

issues.detail: List date 2026-04-01 is taken from PDF metadata (CreationDate), not from the document. The council publishes it as the 2024 local list; the PDF text has no date, and it cites the NPPF of December 2023, so it dates from 2024. The workbook should record 2024 (date basis: link title on the council page).
issues.evidence: Council page link text: 'Planning application requirements local list 2024'; the PDF has no adoption/publication date in its text.

issues.detail: All 12 tab_items come from the generic 'National Planning Application Requirements 2019' guidance, not the local list. None of the 21 local list requirements appear in tab_items. The tab captures only drawing-scale advice and form-submission text.
issues.evidence: Every tab_items source = National-Planning-Application-Requirements-2019-Website-Version.pdf; local list headings run from Affordable Housing Statement to Public Open Space Assessment.

issues.detail: The tab_items are drawing guidance, process text and fragments, not validation requirements. Examples: 8 near-duplicate 'scale should be clearly indicated... Not to Scale will not be accepted' rows with page numbers ('8/15', '9/15') run in; 'Hard copies can be downloaded from the planning website or in the technical help section of this page'; 'Hard copies of the CIL liability form can be downloaded from the Planning Portal'; and a bare label 'European Site (SAC/SPA/Ramsar)' with no requirement.
issues.evidence: tab_items 'Drawing / document standards' x8, 'Submission rules' x3, 'Policy-driven requirements' x1

issues.detail: The same 'scale should be clearly indicated / Not to Scale disclaimers will not be accepted' sentence repeats across 7 of the 8 drawing-standards rows, each with a different run-on fragment.

Several local list items are missing from app_type_rows: (1) Assessment of Proposed Development within Existing Open Space: major residential or mixed development on existing open space. (2) Telecommunication Information: all telecoms development. (3) Evidence for Town Centre Uses / Retail Impact: main town centre uses outside existing centres; retail impact assessment at 350 sqm+ outside the Primary Shopping Area. (4) Public Open Space Assessment: major residential and mixed-use development (only a landscaping fragment is captured). (5) Surface Water Drainage Details: all major and minor full applications and reserved matters. The 'Drainage Strategy / SuDS' row quotes foul-drainage text instead. (6) Assessment of Transport Impact: significant transport implications, all major/minor full and RM, dropped kerbs. Only a 'visibility splays' fragment is captured.
issues.evidence: Local list 2024 headings: 'Assessment of Proposed Development within Existing Open Space', 'Telecommunication Information', 'Evidence for Town Centre Uses', 'Public Open Space Assessment', 'Surface Water Drainage Details', 'Assessment of Transport Impact'

issues.detail: 26 of the 27 Full planning rows carry 'INFERRED: application type not named... placed under Full planning'. Many items in the source apply by threshold or location, or name other types explicitly. Examples: Surface Water Drainage covers reserved matters and has an outline drainage strategy requirement; Transport Impact covers reserved matters; Affordable Housing, Energy, Planning Obligations and Public Open Space apply to major development, including outline. Yet Outline and Reserved matters are both marked '(none) - national requirements only'.
issues.evidence: 'For outline planning applications the applicant should include an outline drainage strategy'; surface water applies 'where details submitted as part of reserved matters submission'

issues.detail: Noise Impact Assessment is placed under Householder as 'Application type named in requirement text'. The Noise item does not mention householder applications; its trigger is noise-sensitive development near noise sources, or noise-generating uses. The excerpt's leading 'householder applications' text bled in from the preceding item.
issues.evidence: Noise item trigger: 'Applications for noise sensitive development including sites adjacent to major road/transport...'; no reference to householder

issues.detail: Three rows sit under Listed building consent only because the text mentions 'listed building'. (1) Lighting Assessment applies to floodlighting or significant external lighting near homes, listed buildings, conservation areas or open countryside; the listed building is a location, not an LBC application type. (2) 'Schedule of works (listed building)' is not a local list item; its excerpt is the Structural Survey text. (3) Structural Survey also covers conversion of rural outbuildings outside settlement boundaries (planning applications).
issues.evidence: 'Proposals involving the provision of publicly accessible developments, in the vicinity of residential property, a listed building or a conservation area, or open countryside'; 'A structural survey may be required... substantial demolition or renovation of a listed building'

issues.detail: 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' is placed under Change of use - prior approval, but its own excerpt says the test is required for applications in Flood Zones 2/3 EXCEPT minor and change of use applications. It also comes from the 2019 national guidance; the 2024 local list has no sequential test item. Likewise, Design and Access Statement is placed under Minerals & waste, although the excerpt says DAS is required for major development EXCLUDING mining and waste development. DAS is a national requirement and South Glos is not a county minerals authority row.
issues.evidence: 'required for all applications within Flood Zones 2 and 3 except for minor and change of use applications'; 'major developments excluding developments for mining operations or waste development'

issues.detail: Many trigger excerpts are fragments that do not state when the item applies. 'Advertisement drawings / illumination details' quotes Lighting Assessment text ('calculations, vertical illuminance, ULR calculations, etc as required'); it is not an advert requirement. Archaeology quotes only the tail of an NPPF paragraph. Heritage Statement = 'in any heritage statement.' (the real trigger is applications in or affecting a conservation area or listed building, excluding change of use, adverts and most householder). Energy = 'provide an energy assessment.' (real trigger: major development, 10+ dwellings or >1000 sqm commercial). Waste = 'sheds and bin stores In the case of minor and major applications cases a site survey will also be required'. Self-build quotes legislation background, not the trigger (custom/self-build sites; residential sites over 100 dwellings). Air Quality starts with an email address 'at SelfBuild@southglos.gov.uk'.
issues.evidence: Energy Statement: 'Major development is defined as 10 or more dwellings or over 1000sqm of commercial space'; Heritage: 'Excludes: Change of use, advertisements, and householder applications unless adjoining or adjacent'

issues.detail: Coal Mining Risk Assessment excerpt describes CMRA content but omits the trigger: all full planning applications except Coal Authority exemptions, in high-risk coal mining areas. Drainage Strategy / SuDS and Foul Sewage rows both quote the same foul-drainage sentence, so the surface water trigger is lost.
issues.evidence: 'All full planning applications excluding those set out in the Coal Authority's exemptions list'

issues.detail: Two rows are not local requirements. 'Environmental Statement (EIA)' quotes a note about including the CMRA within an ES. CIL Additional Information is taken from the 2019 national guidance.
issues.evidence: 'Note - if an environmental statement is required by the ... EIA Regulations 2011 as amended, it is suggested that the CMRA is included within the ES.'

summary: Grokbot's link is the current South Gloucestershire 'Planning application requirements local list 2024' (dated 2024, not 2026-04-01). All its tab_items come from the 2019 national guidance and are mostly drawing and process text. The app-type rows miss several local items (telecoms, town centre/retail impact, open space, surface water, transport) and misplace others under the wrong application types.
